profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a Brussels-based law firm advising a regional hospital alliance spanning Belgium, Germany, and the Netherlands on a memorandum for implementing Directive 2011/24/EU in a Euregio pilot. The team is aligning the public-law/regulatory workstream with the contracting/compliance workstream before circulating a draft coordination memo to the client steering group. The agenda is to confirm what goes into the 'regional cooperation note,' who will supply the legal annexes, which draft text is considered current, and what it means for the package to be 'ready for circulation' by Thursday. The expected outcome is apparent agreement on handoffs, document ownership, and the contents of the circulation package for the client's Friday steering-group pre-read.

members.name: Sophie Lambert
members.expertise: EU patient mobility law, public-sector health cooperation frameworks, regulatory analysis under Directive 2011/24/EU
members.background: French-Belgian lawyer based in Brussels who has spent eight years advising ministries and hospital networks on cross-border care arrangements, especially governance structures and public-law interfaces.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the memo tightly framed around the Directive and avoid opening unresolved reimbursement or procurement issues before the steering group; she is also trying to protect her team's credibility after a late draft last week.
hidden_assumptions: The 'regional cooperation note' means the short board-facing narrative memo plus a high-level legal risks table, not the underlying operational annexes.
The 'latest draft' is the clean Word version she saved after yesterday's call, because tracked internal edits are not yet client-ready and therefore do not count as the working baseline.

If a package is 'ready for circulation,' it is sufficiently complete for the client steering group once the legal position is stable, even if citations are still being normalized and annex placeholders remain.
The reimbursement pathway and patient authorization mechanics are background issues for a later implementation paper unless they are expressly elevated.
Ownership of the common document remains with the regulatory workstream once the main memo frame and headings originated there.

members.name: Jonas Keller
members.expertise: Hospital cooperation agreements, data-sharing clauses, cross-border reimbursement interfaces, implementation documentation for health-sector collaborations
members.background: German-qualified lawyer in the firm's Cologne office who previously worked in-house for a university hospital group coordinating contracts with neighboring-country providers.
members.private_state: He wants the package to be operationally usable by hospital legal departments and to avoid being blamed later for omissions in reimbursement, data-sharing, or referral-routing details; he also assumes the client expects near-final attachments this week.
hidden_assumptions: The 'regional cooperation note' includes the implementation annexes that hospital legal teams will actually rely on, especially the referral flow, reimbursement assumptions, and draft clause schedule.
The 'latest draft' is the shared Teams version with tracked edits and comments from multiple offices, because the collaboration platform is the live source of truth.
A document is only 'ready for circulation' when the package is functionally complete for downstream legal and operational review, including annexes that prevent obvious follow-up questions.

Cross-border reimbursement handling and prior-authorization references are inherent parts of any analysis of when cooperation 'works' under the Directive, even if not highlighted in the meeting invite.
Once a shared client-facing folder exists, ownership of common artifacts is distributed, so each workstream can update the master pack directly.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the regional cooperation note
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to finishing the 'regional cooperation note' for circulation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks this is the core memo: a concise legal narrative on the conditions under which cross-border collaboration can be facilitated under Directive 2011/24/EU, with a brief risks table.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks this includes the core memo plus practical annexes covering referral routing, reimbursement assumptions, and clause placeholders needed for implementation teams.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In law-firm coordination settings, 'note' can naturally mean either the principal memo alone or the full package around it; both participants speak as if the annexes are simply understood parts of the same object.

misalignment_points.topic: Which draft is the latest draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say they will work off the 'latest draft' or 'current draft.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the clean Word draft emailed after yesterday's internal call, which excludes unresolved tracked edits and comments.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the Teams-hosted version 7.3 containing live tracked changes, comment threads, and annex placeholders added by the Cologne and Amsterdam teams.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both documents derive from the same memo and were updated within hours of each other, so the phrase 'latest draft' feels unambiguous; in practice each assumes their usual document-control norm is shared.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the package should be 'ready for circulation' by Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes Thursday readiness means stable client-safe legal framing for the steering group's pre-read, even if annexes are skeletal and footnotes are not fully standardized.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes Thursday readiness means a substantially complete package that downstream hospital counsel can review without immediately requesting missing process documents.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a routine deadline status label rather than a substantive standard, and both are accustomed to high-functioning teams where the implied threshold is rarely spelled out.

misalignment_points.topic: How Jonas will add his input
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree Jonas will 'drop in' the reimbursement and data-sharing pieces this afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects M2 to send short redline language or bullet text for her team to integrate into the memo structure they control.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects to update the shared master file and annex tabs directly in Teams, treating that as the normal way to incorporate his workstream's content.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The expression 'drop in' is colloquial and common in collaborative drafting, masking different assumptions about whether contributions arrive as suggested text or as direct edits to the master file.

If we can say it's ready for circulation by Thursday in the sense of being client-safe for the steering group, that protects us and keeps attention off last week's late draft.
